summary:
Colleague (v1.76.0) is a swappable coder-agent harness — "one runtime, many minds" — that turns model backends into repo workers behind one shared task contract. It is a headless task runtime, not a chat assistant or IDE plugin.

Main parts: the Task/TaskResult contract (colleague/contract.py + contract_* siblings), the bounded tool loop (colleague/loop.py + 26 loop_* modules), repo-confined tools (colleague/tools.py: read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, run_command, culture, devague, subagent, subagents, finish), backend adapters (colleague/engines/), plugin discovery via the colleague.engines entry-point group (colleague/registry.py), the JSON run artifact (colleague/artifact.py), opt-in OpenTelemetry telemetry (colleague/telemetry/), git/PR handoff (colleague/handoff.py), the doctor health check (colleague/oilcheck/), and the checksum-based approval gate (colleague/policy.py). All contract-level features (hooks, telemetry, gates) live in the runtime loop, never in backends — the all-engines rule.

Two bundled backends: mock (deterministic, networkless, contract reference) and vllm-openai (any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint; default model unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4).

Entry points: colleague and clg → colleague.cli:main. Key commands: colleague work "<goal>" --repo ., colleague work --command <name> [args…], colleague (interactive session palette), colleague doctor --probe, colleague learn, colleague learn-from claude, colleague hooks approve, colleague commands list, colleague feedback record/show. Backend resolution: --engine > COLLEAGUE_ENGINE > vllm-openai.

Build/test: hatchling, Python >=3.12, Apache-2.0; one base dep (agentfront>=0.20.0; base install pulls zero third-party transitive deps, enforced by tests/test_zero_deps.py); optional extras [otel], [mcp], [tui], [voice], [resident], [culture]. Tests: uv run pytest -n auto (604 test files); lint: black/isort/flake8/bandit; rubric gate: uv run teken cli doctor . --strict; hard 1000-line file limit; version bump every PR (version-check CI); live vLLM e2e opt-in via COLLEAGUE_VLLM_E2E=1 pytest tests/test_vllm_live.py.

facts.value: Two bundled backends: mock (deterministic, networkless, contract reference, CI workhorse) and vllm-openai (OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with tool calling; default model unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4)
facts.quote: Two backends, both registered through the same colleague.engines entry-point group: mock — deterministic and networkless; the CI workhorse. vllm-openai — drives any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint with tool calling. The built-in default model is unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4.

facts.value: Tool surface: ten tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, run_command, culture, devague, subagent, subagents, finish) as OpenAI function schemas; edit_file is partial-edit; file tools confined to repo root; run_command cwd pinned to root
facts.quote: Ten tools — read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, run_command, culture, devague, subagent, subagents, and finish — are exposed to the model as OpenAI function/tool schemas. ... edit_file (#174) is the partial-edit primitive: an exact-string replace whose cost scales with the change, not the file size.

facts.value: CLI scripts: colleague and clg both → colleague.cli:main; version 1.76.0
Entry points: colleague.engines (mock, vllm-openai) and colleague.renderers (ansi)
All-engines rule: contract behavior must hold identically for every backend; hooks, telemetry, approval gate, pre-finish gates live in the runtime loop (colleague/loop.py), never in engines
facts.quote: The all-engines rule. Behavior that belongs to the contract (task fields, result shape, the loop, the artifact, every runtime-owned feature) must hold identically for every backend. ... Runtime-owned features live in the loop, not in a backend. Hooks, telemetry, the culture/devague tools, the approval gate, work stats, feedback, and the pre-handoff gates ... are owned by colleague/loop.py and the shared execute_work path. A backend module must never reimplement or touch them.

facts.value: Key commands: colleague work "<goal>" --repo .; colleague work --command <name> [args…]; colleague (interactive palette); colleague doctor --probe; colleague learn; colleague learn-from claude
facts.quote: Common commands table: colleague work "<goal>" --repo . — Run a task autonomously through a backend. colleague (no args, at a terminal) — Open the interactive cockpit / session palette. colleague doctor --probe — Check the install and ping the model endpoint. colleague learn — Print a prompt that teaches an agent how to drive colleague. colleague learn-from claude — Absorb another agent's skills into colleague's own.

alternatives.text: Colleague might be primarily a chat assistant or IDE plugin rather than a headless task runtime.
alternatives.predicts: The README and docs would describe interactive chat/IDE integration as the primary use case.
alternatives.refuted_by: f1, f3 — README explicitly states it is not a chat assistant or IDE plugin and is a headless task runtime; commands are work/doctor/session, not chat.

verdicts.text: Colleague is a backend-agnostic, auditable headless coder-agent harness built around a shared Task/TaskResult contract and a bounded tool loop, with two bundled backends (mock and vllm-openai) discovered via entry points, tested via pytest with parallel execution and guarded by zero-deps, all-engines parity, file-length, and boundary tests.
